The same note directs users needing consolidated feeds from all major US exchanges to licensed full-market access.
Free individual API exists and the IEX feed exposes last/best bid/best ask.
Official documentation identifies the feed as IEX TOPS from the IEX Exchange, not consolidated National NBBO across all exchanges.
Finnhub advertises a free realtime US-stock API.
The official realtime websocket endpoint documented for free stock streaming is a trades/last-price stream with symbol, price, timestamp, volume and conditions.
No independent best-bid/best-ask National NBBO quote event with bid/ask timestamps is established by this free websocket evidence.
Current Individual plan starts at $150/month; free access is a trial.
Included EquitiesEdge is proprietary derived/predicted bid-ask-last rather than SIP NBBO.
Other realtime products documented include IEX and Nasdaq Basic; delayed SIP is not fresh G9.
Free-forever plan provides end-of-day data only.
Intraday and real-time US data require paid plans and the documented intraday source is IEX.
Free offer is $125 of historical-data credits, not a permanent realtime entitlement.
Live data requires license activation and pass-through license fees plus usage; usage-based live US Equities is not available.
Benzinga states real-time quotes can be licensed separately and require navigating real-time market-data agreements; no permanent-$0 National NBBO API entitlement is established.
Official product documentation explicitly offers US National Best Bid and Offer from SIP feeds including UTP Tape C and timestamps.
The same product states exchange market-data distribution is subject to licensing requirements and fees and directs users to sales; no permanent-$0 automated/non-display entitlement was found.

interpretation: Free realtime labels commonly resolve to partial-venue, trade-only, delayed, derived, capped/trial, or non-entitled data. Exact SIP/National-NBBO products remain licensed or otherwise fail the strict permanent-zero proof.
